name: security-oauth-dynamic-registration-review
artifacts: Registration endpoint/policy, software statements, redirect URI rules and client metadata consumers.
trace: Determine who may register or modify clients and whether untrusted metadata becomes a trusted redirect, fetch destination or privileged client classification.
experiment: Use an owned local issuer and client; compare permitted registration with one unauthorized metadata mutation and inspect the effective registered client.
disproof: Open registration can be intentional. A client identifier or reflected metadata is not client impersonation or a protected server-side fetch.
repair: Constrain metadata and client class changes at registration/update, then verify intended public clients and rejection of privileged metadata.
branch_decisions: A software statement may authenticate selected metadata, not every caller-supplied field. Inspect registration update authority separately from creation. Open registration and public client classification may be intentional; escalating to a confidential/trusted client or changing another client requires a distinct observed grant.
operational_method: Record any initial-access credential used for creation and the registration-access credential/client URI issued for subsequent management. Those credentials have different scopes and are not interchangeable. Compare updating the created synthetic client with attempting the same operation on a second client; successful open registration alone is not proof of cross-client update authority or confidential-client trust.
